facts.text: Laurelton got its name from the LIRR station, which was christened for the laurels that once lined the area.
The Laurelton Civic Association and Springfield Gardens–Laurelton Historical Society work to preserve historic homes and keep the tree canopy thriving.
Laurelton’s LIRR station near 225th Street and 141st Road offers a direct rail link straight into Manhattan.
Dean Alvord built Laurelton in the 1920s, designing it after an English village with Tudor‑style homes.
Many Laurelton streets feature landscaped center malls, giving the neighborhood a distinctly tree‑lined, pedestrian‑friendly feel.
From the 1930s through the 1970s, Laurelton hosted a vibrant Jewish‑American community before becoming a hub for African‑American, Caribbean, and West African residents.
